cr_data.provenance: (The Downtown Gallery, New York, NY); Private collection, Miami, Florida, 1950; Descended in family (Source: Lynes, 1999)
remarks_1999: Double entries Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive. Whitney Archive titles work *White Barn No. 4* and indicates, "Exam. at Amer. Place, March 1946. . . . No signature. On backing: Title and date as above. On backing: Downtown Gallery label. Similar to other 1932 barns but has a lean–to built on right end." Another Whitney Archive fact sheet indicates, "Note: I have dated this 1932 as it belongs to the 1932 group of white barns." Same Whitney Archive fact sheet titles work *White Barn with Cart*, but provides a drawing of work that includes the cart and the lean–to described on the other Whitney Archive fact sheet. Downtown Gallery Archive titles work *White Barn No. IV* and provides dimensions: "11 3/4 x 29 3/4." Another fact sheet in Downtown Gallery Archive titles work *White Barn with Cart*, includes no dimensions, but provides a photograph of work whose characteristics match those described on fact sheet in Whitney Archive with title *White Barn with Cart*. Downtown Gallery Archive indicates the picture was in "Coll. Museum of Modern Art," but it was only on approval at MOMA temporarily in the 1930s. The Downtown Gallery label mentioned in Whitney Archive whose title might resolve this issue is lost. Abiquiú Notebooks indicates, "Sold by Downtown Gallery fall of 1950." This work, cat. no. 807 or cat. no. 809 was possibly no. 14 in 1933 New York (An American Place) exhibition; see cat. nos. 805–7, 809. Reproduced and titled *White Barn with Cart in *Studio* (January 1937). (Source: Lynes, 1999)

description: Two small and two large brown doors punctuate the surface of a barn's smooth white wall. The barn has a pitched black roof. A brown cart stands inside it. Above the building is a bright blue sky.
title: White Barn with Cart
